newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela wants more Colombian presence on border.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela wants more Colombian presence on border.

text.p: Venezuela's President Rafael Caldera called on Colombia to increase its presence along their shared border, an area which "is controlled by guerrillas, drug traffickers and terrorists."
In a rare interview with leading local daily El Universal, Caldera said subversive groups in Colombia were creating serious headaches for his government.
"The authorities elected in border departments and municipalities in Colombia are considered to be at the very least sympathetic to these groups," he said.
Venezuela and Colombia frequently exchange diplomatic barbs over incidents along their 1,250 mile- (2,000 km-) long border where kidnapping, drug trafficking and smuggling is common.

"Colombia's political organisation means that the army has the fundamental obligation to guard the most populated areas of the country such as Bogota and Medellin and lacks sufficient resources to maintain a presence in the border regions," Caldera said.

Caldera, 80, said the level of tension at the border meant that for the first time in the two countries' history Venezuela was not only unconcerned by a Colombian military presence at the border, "but rather we ask Colombia for this presence as a guarantee of control."
